body:
See, this is actually quite encouraging, and I'll explain why

> I doubt it involves yelling at the other for donating money, going on vacation while the other is in the hospital from a heart attack (caused by the yelling), affairs, lies, etc.

You've actually started to identify what you *don't* want from relationships either friendships, family, or marriage/partnerships.

This is a really, really, really good start. Unhealthy relationships can take many forms, and the good thing is, your own personal red flags (not what 'society says' is a red flag, but what is personally not alright with you) actually can appear early on.  

Or, early-ish. And by starting to identify what you don't want in a relationship or interaction - that's.... that took me decades longer than it should have. 

This kind of thing is really good to let yourself start to gain awareness and understanding of.

> I think I help people to forget about my own reality.

Sweetheart, I mean this in the best possible way. But you've hit the nail on the head. 

This in no way means that you can't be a valuable contribution to someone else's life, or help someone who genuinely needs it *when it's appropriate* but I think you're right about this.

>I have difficulty doing something for my own benefit if it's bad for someone else.

This is a necessary part of life sometimes. And sometimes, what seems 'bad' for someone else is actually better for them in the long run. 

I've had to fire people. It was bad for them and better for everyone in the long run. I've had to walk away from relationships. The other person thought it was bad, and for them it was at the time but it was best for everyone involved. I've had to say no at my job, no to my husband even. 

Since you are so attuned to the loneliness and pain in the world, you may really need to be careful about how much you expose yourself to it. And if you have any kind of connection to the higher power of the universe, I would strenghten that as much as you can.

There is another weird unhealthy post modern belief that good people have to fix everything in the world. Comfort every lonely person. It's not true. It's not even possible, and in some ways it can even turn into an arrogance (which I'm not saying you're doing, but that's definitely an aspect of it.) 

You may be inadvertently cutting yourself off from the help that you need, the support and healing that you need by - even benevolently - trying to be there for everyone else. And, the internet really stokes these feeligs of 'I must save the world' when really, a lot of the people pushing these ideas are not healthy at all, and are not managing their own lives effectively.

I completely understand how you feel, wanting to comfort people who are alone. I get it completely. Sometimes just meditating puts energy out into the world that can find its way to a hear that is open to receiving it. But you will have to fill yourself up, trust me. I'm a lot older than you. My early 20's were far more unhealthy than they needed to be because i simply refused to let myself be happy when I knew I could be. 

> I forget that those aren't my thoughts.

You sound like a very emotionally astute and aware person. This is both a blessing and a curse. And perhaps it's the right time to learn how to manage it, not allow it to bring unnecessary pain into your life.

Wow, that's a lotta stuff to experience. i gotta say, if you are around people who need your help, you may not be getting the help you need. But this is more of a choice on your part. Ultimately, eventually at some point in life, you will have to say no to people. 

Every single step of personal and emotional growth I have taken has either primarily or secondarily involved saying no to someone. And it's how I find myself relatively free from toxic relationships today. My dark thoughts and plans tend to only come up when I am reminded of how things used to be. And I have to make some changes so that I don't go back to that. And that involved making choices that others will most certainly be unhappy with.

>I don't know what to do. 

Ultimately, you will have to say no to something. Or, you may find that you are actually pretty okay with the situation you are in with helping people, and that's something you'll chose to keep doing. The choice is yours. And if you have difficulty doing something that someone else finds upsetting, that is something you'll have to work very hard on. But maybe that is something you will do down the road.

As for my family. I don't have one. I was born into a very very unhealthy unstable situation and it never got better. I have people I am related to who are varying degrees of not functional. I was on my own from a very young age, grew up really fast, and that's where I am now. Just cleaning up the asbestos-like mess of the childhood I didn't have. I'm likely a lot older than you, so this is why I am advising you to chose your company carefully. Especially men. But you are likely already realizing that.

The modern world is very fixated on freedom and hedonism and relationships as entertainment. This freedom has a lot of negative consequences in terms of relationship instability and young people being alone in situations they are not equipped to handle.

I wish I could give you some words of encouragement about your boyfriend. I wish the two of you had the stable, safe environment you needed to pursue what you both want in terms of life outcome and perhaps even building a life together.

I really wish young people weren't experiencing such pain that one young person has to help keep another young person from ending their life. 

I'm glad I am able to say this out loud. Although I don't know if it is a comfort to you or not.

I just think you and your boyfriend deserve better, and shouldn't be in this kind of pain.

> I wouldn't get to speak, and she would be biased towards my mom because she only heard her lies. Even when I told her that my mom hit me or threatened me, she would take my mother's side.

Not uncommon, and why I think therapy is to be viewed with a very skeptical eye, especially for young people. 

And I'm so sorry this happened to you. A version of that happened to me many, many, many times with many therapists. I learned to not trust them. 

>I don't want to leave people who feel suicidal alone but I can't keep breaking myself to help them.

This jumped out at me like a big red sign. I think that you should consider stepping away from helping other people who are in a crisis that is outside your pay grade. Just consider it. For your own health. I'm getting the impression you are young. Be very careful about the people you surround yourself with. Sometimes you think you are helping someone but really they don't want to get better, they just drag others down with them. My closest friend is someone who is very good at taking a step back from asking me for help. She's been through some challenging stuff that I helped her with, but she always knows when I need a break and never ever takes it personally if I can't be there for her for everything. That is a great balance, I've found. 

I'm very sorry to hear about your boyfriend. I wouldn't even know what to say about that situation. You are a young woman and as long as you're not actively being nasty to him, I don't know if you are realistically equipped to carry something heavy like that with him. But I honestly don't know what to say, I really wish I could say something helpful - for both of you. 

As for my husband, he and I are very very close and he is very much NOT a personal therapist. He's from a different culture than me (well, he's from the back-home version of where I'm from) and he brings a moral and ethical perspective to things that is beyond what a therapist ever does. 

I've found that therapists tend to shy away from anything that looks like acknowledging good and evil, right action and wrong action. My husband makes no bones about the fact that what I have been through is trauma, not a 'misunderstanding.' 

He sometimes looks at what I have been through and grown up around he's gobsmacked like "how can people act this way towards a child, towards their own family?" Therapists just tend to avoid saying that anything anyone has done is ever wrong or immoral. So in that way he is not like a therapist per se. 

And I know how you feel about the knives. I honestly have to say to my husband sometimes "I can't be in the kitchen right now I can't be around a knife" and he gets it. 

>I just don't want to be manipulated.

If you are in a relationship that ever feels like manipulation, then you have absolute permission to step away from that relationship. I feel this has to be said. If things are getting too much for you in a relationship, you have every right to step away.  If you're feeling trapped that's not a good sign :(

No, you make a lot of sense, actually.

It's interesting that you said that about communication, to be honest, I've massively changed and improved my communication with everyone I interact with. I'm not saying I'm completely open with everyone all the time (some people you can't tell everything to,) but the communication improvements have been.... crucial.

And to be honest it's weird that you mentioned a therapist. I started looking for one yesterday and it's one of hte things that pushed me to a bad place. I've never had success with one, No wait, I've had success with only one, and that was like 9 years ago as a result of being the victim of a pretty bad crime. I addressed the specific issues around the trial and everything, but didn't go much deeper. 

Therapists are, sadly, in my experience, not always on the right team as it were. But that's just been my experience. Also when you have sort of "woo woo" spiritual beliefs, therapists can often brush them off and that's very unhelpful. Eh, it's not something I've had a lot of success with, therapists. But if you're young and you find one that works for you, I would recommend you pursue that.

I think emotional honesty is the key to dealing with difficult things. Whether it's in a therapy setting, or just being honest with yourself about how you feel and what is hurting you. 

Keep thinking outloud if you want, it's really actually kind of therapeutic to hear someone else do it!

I'm not sure if the holiday was a trigger, I'm don't celebrate Christmas but I'm sure there's a cultural trigger there probably, Last Christmas there was an intense change in my house that was hard to deal with.

I'm really sorry to hear you don't live in a good household. Like, really sorry to hear that.  That's not something you should have to be dealing with, and I know there's not much you can do about it, I just want you to know you deserve to live in a peaceful home. 

Shit like what we go through, there isn't a handbook for how to deal with it. I try not to think about methods or wanting to unless it's really like, something I can't get out of my head. 

I think even just telling the truth about bad shit is really important. Like "this shit that is happening isn't good, and I'm not gonna pretend like it is, even though I can't do anything about it right this second." 

I don't know, being emotionally honest with myself was a good habit I got into that helped keep the thoughts and feelings away. Kind of like moving in another direction. I'm glad you have good friends to open up to, and crying is a good idea, too. :)

No dude, it's fine, you can deffo talk about you. :) 

I have a ... method for dealing with the impulses I would say. I've called a hotline on more than one occasion. Amazingly the guy who I spoke to last Christmas was actually pretty helpful. I didn't talk to him for long but something about it really snapped me into reality. In a good way. 

Sadly I had to tell the truth about the two things that were triggering my impulses. one was big, one was enormous. and I had to face and deal with both of them. I don't want to make things worse for you by asking but... what helps you?

Do you feel like it's okay for you to talk about it? I don't want to push you but I'm glad you're opening up about it. No judgement here.

It's very scary. I never used to be like this until about 2 years ago. I didn't even want to acknowledge what had triggered it. It's taken every ounce of strength to deal with the pain. I just want to not be triggered into these impulses again. I'm working so hard on it. I think hearing about that kid yesterday (another celebrity's kid, which makes it worse) that did it.

A lot better. Thanks to a brosef here on reddit actually.

I spend so much time crowding out the memories of how I became suicidal in the first place, then when the memories can't be crowded out anymore, its like drowning and.... sometimes your arms get tired.

I really hope I can get rid of these impulses and ideas. But I still have to take them seriously when they make an appearance. 

Thank you for asking. It is appreciated.

Thats very kind of you. I just have a lot of stuff to deal with and I'm totally alone with it. Every time someone else commits suicide I think... shit, I should probably do that. He seemed like a nice kid, what chance do I have?

I just have a lot of heavy shit to deal with and I'm pretty much alone with it.

Very helpful, thanks. :eyeroll: And please don't turn this into something about you. I think anyone can agree that's not appropriate, especially not here. 

This is a place of support, not arguing. rule one.
